featured_reviews.name: Dr. Aman Bhonsle
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been coming here since I was a kid—long enough that I’m pretty sure my first real chicken tandoori happened right here. The menu has changed over the years, sure, but the place has stubbornly refused to lose its old-school charm. Portions? Still generous. This isn’t food that apologizes for itself.

The Chinese starters have absolutely nothing to do with China—and thank God for that. They’re loud, greasy, Indo-Chinese comfort bombs that slap hard. Pick any of the chicken gravies and you’re in a good place emotionally. I will say this: the kebabs feel a little smaller than they used to. Shrinkflation? Age? Betrayal? I don’t know. Still good. Just… noted.

Twenty-one years ago, when I was a broke college student and my parents would leave town—trusting me alone at home far more than they should have—I ordered from here like it was a civic duty. My friends from that era still remember how much food I could put away from this place. This is not health food. No one here is pretending otherwise. But it hits all the right buttons.

I ordered so often that before food apps, before algorithms, the guy answering the phone knew my order just by hearing my voice. Within an hour, like clockwork, the food would land at my parents’ place. I’d sit there demolishing it while binge-watching American TV, living my best irresponsible life.

Some of my old favorites are gone now, but the current menu holds its own. I’ve eaten here with my wife, with her family, across decades and phases of life. Parking is usually manageable. There’s a mosque nearby, Bombay Hospital around the corner, and the now-shuttered Liberty Cinema—where I watched half my childhood movies. The area isn’t glamorous. It doesn’t try to be. It’s old Mumbai, still breathing, still feeding people properly.

This place survives because it’s trusted. Because it’s consistent. Because people who know food still show up here quietly and eat without drama.

What’s instantly noticeable is who eats here.
Old-school locals, serious food people, and a steady stream of expats—especially Arab expats—who clearly didn’t wander in by accident.

Late at night, you’ll see many happy Muslim families settling in comfortably, sharing plates, unhurried, treating the place like an extension of home.

Go without hesitation.
Ask the manager what to order.

Then sit down and let them take care of you.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited McDonald's CSMT near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, and it was a convenient stop in the middle of a busy day in South Mumbai. The outlet is located in a prime area, making it an easy choice for travelers, office workers, and students looking for a quick and reliable meal. Due to its central location, the place is usually crowded, but the system runs smoothly.

The service here is completely self-service. You place your order at the counter or digital kiosk, wait for your token number, and collect your tray once it’s ready. Even during rush hours, the process is quite organized, and the staff handles the crowd efficiently. The waiting time was reasonable, and the order was served fresh.

We ordered a chicken burger combo, cheesy fries, Oreo shake, and a Mc coffee cappuccino. The chicken burger combo was satisfying, with a soft bun and a crispy chicken patty that had the familiar McDonald’s taste. The fries served with the combo were fresh and crispy. The cheesy fries were a highlight, topped with warm, creamy cheese sauce that added extra flavor and made them more indulgent.

The Oreo shake was thick, chilled, and perfectly sweet, making it a refreshing treat. It had a good blend of Oreo flavor and creamy texture. The Mc coffee cappuccino was nicely prepared, with a smooth texture and balanced coffee taste, perfect to relax after a long day.

The taste overall follows their standard franchise model, which means you get consistent flavors just like any other McDonald’s outlet. The seating area is decent, though it can feel a bit crowded during peak hours. Cleanliness is maintained well, and tables are cleared regularly.

Overall, it was a satisfying experience for a quick meal near CSMT. My rating for this outlet is 4 out of 5.

featured_reviews.name: ROHAN REDEKAR
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you want to eat authentic and affordable pav bhaji in a bustling city like Mumbai, Lenin Pav Bhaji is a must-try place. This place is famous for its bhaji made with Amul Maska and for its reasonable prices. Every customer who comes here feels the taste of the real Mumbai streets with the first bite.

The main identity of Lenin Pav Bhaji is their bhaji dipped in Amul butter. Fresh vegetables — potatoes, peas, tomatoes, bell peppers, and a wonderful blend of spices — are used while preparing the bhaji. The generous use of Amul Maska on it gives the bhaji a creamy, aromatic, and satisfying taste. The crispy pav roasted on a tava, melted butter on top, and a lemon wedge served with it — this experience attracts every customer again and again.

The prices here are another big feature.  The plain pav bhaji costs around ₹70–₹90, while the special Amul pav bhaji costs around ₹110–₹120. These prices are really affordable for such quality taste. This makes this place a good choice for students, workers, and families.

The service is fast, the staff is polite, and the place is always kept clean. Even in a crowded place, the taste and quality are maintained, which is the success of Lenin pav bhaji.

Overall, Lenin pav bhaji is the perfect blend of authentic Mumbai street food, the magic of Amul mask, and affordable pleasure. This place scores 10 out of 10 in all three aspects - taste, quality, and price.

Honestly, this place was a complete disappointment. I already had doubts before going there, but my friends insisted we give it a try. The moment I reached, I could tell it was one of those overhyped places made popular through random influencer reels rather than actual good food.

We took a parcel and ordered:

**Za'atar Naan with Hummus** – The naan was decent mainly because it was loaded with cheese, so that saved the dish a bit. Otherwise, nothing special.

**Hummus** – Completely bland. No flavour, no seasoning, literally tasted like raw hummus ,they forgot salt exists.

**Changezi Tikka** – Total waste of money. Again, the same issue — no salt, no proper spices, no flavour at all. This is such a basic dish and easily available at so many places, so at least for the price they charge, it should have been good… but it wasn’t even close.

If they can’t get simple dishes right, I honestly doubt the rest of the menu would be any better. The food felt like it was just mass-produced without anyone even checking how it actually tastes before serving.

A Profoundly Disappointing Culinary Experience

My recent visit to Restaurant Shiv Sagar was, without hyperbole, one of the most profoundly disappointing culinary experiences I have ever endured. This establishment fails catastrophically on every metric that defines a worthwhile restaurant, from the moment you sit down until the moment you thankfully leave. I feel compelled to provide a candid account to ensure fellow diners can make an informed choice and avoid the regret we felt.

The most critical failure lies, undoubtedly, with the food. To simply call it subpar would be a significant understatement; it was, quite frankly, one of the worst meals I have ever consumed. Each dish we ordered was a masterclass in mediocrity, lacking any discernible freshness, flavour, or culinary care. The spices were either absent or jarringly unbalanced, and the overall impression was of food that had been prepared with a sheer lack of interest, tasting bland, pre-made, and carelessly reheated. It was an absolute letdown that formed the core of our negative experience.

This culinary disaster was perfectly complemented by an equally dismal physical environment. The ambiance is best described as poor, with a cramped, cluttered, and uninspiring layout. A significant and frustrating practical issue was the size of the tables. They are inexplicably tiny, making it a genuine struggle to accommodate two plates of food alongside basic essentials like water glasses, condiments, and cutlery. This created a constant, uncomfortable juggling act throughout the meal, completely destroying any possibility of a relaxed dining atmosphere.

To complete this trifecta of failure, the service was exceptionally poor. The staff were inattentive, disinterested, and painfully slow. We waited an eternity to place our order, another eternity for the food to arrive, and a final eternity to receive the bill and settle the payment. Simple requests, like a refill of water, were met with indifference and long delays. The complete absence of basic hospitality was the final straw. In conclusion, Restaurant Shiv Sagar offers no compelling reason for a visit. I cannot recommend it and will unequivocally not be returning.
